q: The entropy compression method (introduced in combinatorics) is an information-theoretic technique for proving existence results. It works by showing:
opts: The entropy of the output is maximized
If a random process terminates, then the entropy of the algorithm's execution must be bounded—forcing termination
Randomized algorithms have lower entropy than deterministic ones
exp: Entropy compression: if an algorithm can be 'compressed' (the random transcript can be reconstructed from a smaller encoding), then the information-theoretic bound forces the algorithm to terminate. Used by Moser-Tardos to prove the constructive Lovász Local Lemma.
